hero.title: Software that leaves evidence.
hero.subtitle: Build systems that can explain what they did, why they did it, who or what caused it, and what humans or agents can safely do next — without reconstructing the story from logs.

beats.label: logs
beats.text: Logs tell you what happened — a pile of facts with no thread.

beats.label: trace
beats.text: A trace puts the facts in order — you can follow the path.

beats.label: causal trace
beats.text: A causal trace keeps the decisions — every fork your system took, and why it took it.

beats.label: the payoff
beats.text: Which means you can ask your app follow-up questions — and it answers from its own record.

story.closing: No extra instrumentation — the structure your app runs on is the structure that explains it.

hero.title: The provenance-native ecosystem.
hero.subtitle: Execution, context, capabilities, and exploration are recorded structurally at runtime so causes can be sliced, replayed, compared, and rendered without reconstructing them from logs.

beats.label: logs
beats.text: Logs are unstructured emissions — raw data of what happened, useful only forensically.

beats.label: trace
beats.text: A trace records execution order — which steps ran, in what sequence.

beats.label: causal trace
beats.text: A causal trace captures the decision structure — every branch condition, its evidence, and read/write provenance — collected as the chart runs, never reconstructed after.

beats.label: the payoff
beats.text: The commit log becomes a queryable substrate: an LLM walks the same structure that executed, so answers cite decisions, not guesses.

story.closing: The fluent builder emits the chart; one traversal executes it and captures everything — the shape that runs is the shape that answers.

map.heading: Two ecosystems, one law

map.evidenceSubline: each library records its own causal trace — same law, no shared runtime

idea.lead: Different systems produce different typed footprints, but every implementation follows the same rule: create the evidence inline, never infer it afterward.

steps.title: Record at traversal time

steps.title: Preserve causal structure
steps.description: Linear runs, parent-linked trails, and capability graphs retain dependencies, principals, branches, and rejected actions.

steps.title: Compose evidence consumers
steps.description: Slicing, replay, comparison, MCP tools, and React lenses operate on the recorded structure instead of parsing logs.

idea.quote: Inline recording is truth. Post-processing is reconstruction.

business.label: Business

hero.title: Software that leaves evidence.
hero.subtitle: Your systems already do the work. These libraries make them keep the reasons — so a customer's follow-up is answered from the record instead of becoming a ticket, an incident is read instead of reconstructed, and the decisions that need a person are the only ones that wait for one.

business.solarCaption: viewed through Flow, Why, and Story — one record, whoever is asking

beats.label: logs
beats.text: Logs are a pile of facts. Putting them back in order is work someone is paid to do, after the fact.

beats.label: trace
beats.text: A trace puts the facts in order. You can see what happened — you still cannot see why it happened.

beats.label: causal trace
beats.text: A causal trace keeps the decisions: the call the system made, the evidence behind it, who or what asked for it, and what it cost.

beats.label: the payoff
beats.text: So the follow-up question — why did you tell me that? — is answered from the record, with the reason cited, instead of becoming an escalation.

story.closing: No separate audit system to buy or keep in sync — the structure the work already runs on is the structure that explains it.

idea.quote: The work stays the same. The evidence is what you keep.

product.title: Understand a backend decision
product.description: Rewind any output or state value to the reads, writes, branches, and routing decisions that produced it.

technical.title: Execution provenance runtime
technical.description: A pre-declared flowchart runtime with transactional state, typed reads and writes, decision evidence, variable-first backward slicing, replay, and generated tool descriptions.

business.title: Trace any outcome back to the decision behind it
business.description: Every run keeps what it read, the path it took, and why it took that path — so a disputed price, refund, or routing is looked up instead of reconstructed. Reconstructing it is the expensive part.

product.title: Debug why your agent failed
product.description: Find the context that changed an answer, narrow the suspects, remove one, replay the run, and prove whether it caused the failure.

technical.title: Context provenance runtime
technical.description: Captures context injections, execution state, decisions, model calls, tools, and cost; slicing, influence ranking, ablation, and counterfactual replay localize failures.

business.title: Your agent can answer the follow-up question
business.description: An agent that keeps its causal trace can say what it used, what it chose, and what it cost — so "why did you tell me that?" gets a cited answer from the record instead of becoming a ticket.

product.title: Make applications agent-operable
product.description: Give agents a typed map of the app's real capabilities while preserving permissions, confirmation gates, and the signed-in user's control.

technical.title: Typed capability and action graph
technical.description: Exposes live application capabilities as a typed skill graph over MCP, with preconditions, permissions, guide mode, action boundaries, and confirmation gates.

business.title: Let agents operate your app — inside the gates you already have
business.description: Agents act through the app's real permissions and confirmation gates. The calls that need a person come with the evidence to decide on; the routine ones prove themselves.

product.title: Preserve every exploration path
product.description: Keep every human and agent branch of an analysis, compare paths, replay findings, and preserve statistical obligations even when a path is abandoned.

technical.title: Branchable exploration provenance
technical.description: Append-only parent-linked commits, mixed-principal causes, named branches, comparison, replay and adoption, declared analyses, and a shared online-FDR ledger.

business.title: Show how a number was arrived at
business.description: Every path a person or an agent explored is kept, including the ones abandoned — so a figure in a report can be shown with the work behind it, and a reviewer can follow the same route.

product.title: every step: watch the flowchart unfold
product.description: Inspect the flowchart, time-travel through the run, and rewind any variable to its origin on the same timeline.

technical.title: every step: watch the flowchart unfold
technical.description: Themeable React components for flowchart traversal, transactional state, time travel, and causal rewind over the footprintjs execution record.

business.title: every step: read the run, not the logs
business.description: Engineers walk the recorded run — each step, each value, each branch — instead of rebuilding the incident from logs. The rebuilding is the part you pay for.

product.title: grouped by what matters: pinpoint why this answer
product.description: Move through messages, prompts, tools, decisions, and cost with one time cursor while you test the suspected cause.

technical.title: grouped by what matters: pinpoint why this answer
technical.description: A React debugger that aligns messages, prompts, tool calls, decision scope, causal slices, and cost on one execution cursor.

business.title: grouped by what matters: find the cause and test it
business.description: Messages, prompts, tools, decisions, and spend sit on one timeline — so a suspected cause can be removed, the run repeated, and the claim settled instead of argued.

product.title: the story: explain it to a person
product.description: Replay reasoning, evidence, tools, and alternatives as an animated story a person can scrub, inspect, and challenge.

technical.title: the story: explain it to a person
technical.description: A build-free, scrubbable role replay that consumes agentfootprint evidence and exposes scored alternatives behind each tool choice.

business.title: the story: explain it to a person
business.description: Replay what the system did as a story a customer-facing team, a reviewer, or a manager can follow — and push back on — without reading a log.
